title: Kummer pole calculus
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] with fraction field $F$ [def-pc-field-extension] of characteristic zero and residue characteristic a prime $p$. Suppose $\zeta\in R$ has multiplicative order $p$. Put $w=1-\zeta$, let $v:F^\times\to\mathbf Z$ be the valuation normalized to take a uniformizer to $1$, set $v(0)=+\infty$, and write $e=v(w)>0$. The polynomial $P(T)=((1+wT)^p-1)/w^p$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] is monic in $R[T]$ and has the form $P(T)=T^p-T+\sum_{1\leq i<p}a_iT^i$ with every $a_i\in wR$. One has $v(p)=(p-1)e$ and the polynomial identity $P(X+Y+wXY)=P(X)+P(Y)+w^pP(X)P(Y)$. For every integer $0\leq n<pe$ and $c\in F$ with $v(c)\geq-n/p$, one has $v(P(c))\geq-n$, $v(P(c)-(c^p-c))\geq e-n$, and $v(wc)>0$. For $x,y\in F$ with $v(x),v(y)\geq-n$, one has $v(w^pxy)\geq pe-2n$. If $E/F$ is any field extension, $z\in E$, and $1+wc\ne0$, then $F(z+c+wzc)=F(z)$, where $F(z)$ denotes the subfield generated by $F$ and $z$.

source.place: Tag 09F2, lemma-prepare, and Tag 09F5, lemma-lowering-the-level, equations first-congruence and second-congruence (with the valuation hypothesis corrected to pi^n P(c) integral).

proof.text: Write $k=R/\mathfrak m$. The Frobenius formula of [def-weil-ring-frobenius] gives $(\bar\zeta-1)^p=\bar\zeta^p-1=0$ in the field $k$, hence $\bar\zeta=1$. Exact order $p>1$ gives $w\ne0$, and $w\in\mathfrak m$. Valuation conventions, with $v(0)=\infty$: [lem-sc-dvr-valuation-arithmetic] gives $v(ab)=v(a)+v(b)$, hence $v(1)=0$; [lem-sc-dvr-valuation-ring-characterization] and [lem-sc-dvr-nonnegative-valuation-in-ring] give $R=\{a:v(a)\geq0\}$. If $a\in R$ is a unit, $v(a)+v(a^{-1})=0$ with both terms $\geq0$, so $v(a)=0$; if $a\in R$ has $v(a)=0$, then $v(a^{-1})=0$ and $a^{-1}\in R$. Since $R$ is local, $\mathfrak m=\{a:v(a)>0\}$; in particular $e=v(w)>0$. For nonzero $a,b$ with $a+b\ne0$ and $v(a)\leq v(b)$: $v(b/a)\geq0$ gives $1+b/a\in R$, so $v(a+b)=v(a)+v(1+b/a)\geq v(a)$. Thus $v(a+b)\geq\min(v(a),v(b))$, and finite-sum bounds follow by repeating it.

source.place: Tag 09F2, lemma-prepare, proof; local binomial calculation in place of cyclotomic factorization.

proof.text: For $1\leq i<p$, the prime-binomial divisibility stated in [def-weil-ring-frobenius] gives integers $b_i=\binom pi/p$, with $b_1=1$. Expand $0=(1-w)^p-1$ by [lem-pur-commutative-ring-binomial-expansion] and cancel the nonzero factor $-w$ in $F$. The result is $pU=(-1)^p w^{p-1}$, where $U=1+\sum_{i=2}^{p-1}b_i(-w)^{i-1}\in1+wR$. Because $w\in\mathfrak m$, $U$ has residue $1$ and is a unit of the local ring $R$. Thus $u=p/w^{p-1}=(-1)^pU^{-1}\in R^\times$, and taking valuations gives $v(p)=(p-1)e$.

source.place: Tag 09F2, lemma-prepare, proof; local binomial calculation in place of cyclotomic factorization.

proof.text: Expand $(1+wT)^p$ using [lem-pur-commutative-ring-binomial-expansion]. The constant term of $P$ is zero, its leading coefficient is $1$, and its coefficient of $T^i$, for $1\leq i<p$, is $\binom pi w^{i-p}=b_i u w^{i-1}$. These coefficients lie in $R$; those with $i\geq2$ lie in $wR$. Also $u-(-1)^p=(-1)^p(1-U)U^{-1}\in wR$. If $p$ is odd this says $u+1\in wR$; if $p=2$, $u-1\in wR$ and $2=p=uw\in wR$, so again $u+1\in wR$. Taking $a_1=u+1$ and $a_i=b_iuw^{i-1}$ for $2\leq i<p$ proves exactly the asserted monic shape, including $p=2$.

source.place: Tag 09F2, lemma-prepare, proof; local binomial calculation in place of cyclotomic factorization.

proof.text: Put $S=X+Y+wXY$. Since $1+wS=(1+wX)(1+wY)$, the definition of $P$ gives $1+w^pP(S)=(1+w^pP(X))(1+w^pP(Y))$. Subtract $1$ and cancel the nonzero scalar $w^p$ in $F[X,Y]$ to obtain $P(S)=P(X)+P(Y)+w^pP(X)P(Y)$. All its coefficients are in $R$ by the preceding step, so this is also the required identity over $R$.

source.place: Tag 09F2, lemma-prepare, final polynomial identity; omitted direct computation written out.

proof.text: Fix $0\leq n<pe$ and $c\in F$ with $t=v(c)\geq-n/p$. If $c=0$, the three assertions follow from $P(0)=0$ and $v(0)=\infty$. Otherwise $v(c^p)=pt\geq-n$, $t\geq-n$, and, for $1\leq i<p$, $v(a_ic^i)\geq e+it\geq e-in/p\geq e-n$. Repeated use of the valuation inequality gives $v(P(c)-(c^p-c))\geq e-n$ and then $v(P(c))\geq-n$. Finally $v(wc)=e+t\geq e-n/p>0$; hence $1+wc$ has residue $1$ and is nonzero.

source.place: Tag 09F5, lemma-lowering-the-level, equation-first-congruence; explicit estimates from the shape established above.

proof.text: For $x,y\in F$ with $v(x),v(y)\geq-n$, if either is zero the bound is immediate. Otherwise multiplicativity gives $v(w^pxy)=pe+v(x)+v(y)\geq pe-2n$.

For any field extension $E/F$, any $c\in F$ and $z\in E$ with $1+wc\ne0$, put $z_c=z+c+wzc=c+(1+wc)z$. Since its coefficients belong to $F$, $z_c\in F(z)$. Conversely $z=(z_c-c)/(1+wc)\in F(z_c)$. The two inclusions of generated subfields give $F(z_c)=F(z)$.

source.place: Tag 09F5, lemma-lowering-the-level, translations of a generating element; explicit inverse affine formula.
